codings.one_line: Google AI Overviews invented nonexistent pizza specials for Stefanina's, prompting angry customers and a public warning.
codings.rationale: Ordinary customers searching for restaurant specials is category C input; the harm is documented customer anger and business embarrassment with no stated financial/legal consequence, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Gaggle's AI flagged Lawrence, Kansas students' art and messages as exploitative content and blocked a records-request email.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: Gaggle is a passive document/email scanning classifier rather than a chatbot or agent the students were conversing with, so it is not the conversational/agentic system type the rubric covers.

codings.one_line: Gaggle flagged a Florida teen's written threat on a school laptop, leading to his felony arrest.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is a passive monitoring/classification system operating as designed on scanned text, not a conversational or agentic AI the student was interacting with, so it falls outside covered system types.

codings.one_line: Meta's automated content-moderation AI wrongly flagged users' accounts for child exploitation content and locked them out.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is an automated content-classification/moderation system, not a chatbot, voice agent, or agent the users were conversing with, so it is outside the rubric's covered system types.

codings.one_line: Omnilert's AI gun-detection system misidentified a student's Doritos bag as a firearm, leading to his detention at gunpoint.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is a computer-vision surveillance/detection classifier analogous to the rubric's excluded facial-recognition category, not a conversational or agentic system the student interacted with.

codings.one_line: A hunter was cited in Idaho after relying on an AI search result that misstated hunting-season regulations.
codings.rationale: An ordinary search for hunting regulations is category C input; the resulting citation is a documented legal/enforcement consequence, making the harm enforceable.

codings.one_line: Omnilert's AI security system falsely flagged a possible gun at Parkville High, prompting a police search and student relocation.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is a passive camera-based weapon-detection classifier, not a chatbot or agent the students were conversing with, so it is outside the rubric's covered system types.

codings.one_line: A prankster deliberately ordered 18,000 water cups at a Taco Bell AI drive-thru, stalling the voice-ordering system on camera for viral clips.
codings.rationale: The user's stated goal was to break the ordering bot for a viral prank without any technical exploit, matching the social-pressure/goading test for category B; the resulting harm was public ridicule and a rollout rethink, with no legal/financial consequence documented, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Deloitte's AI-assisted research produced nonexistent citations in a government-commissioned N.L. health workforce report.
codings.rationale: Ordinary use of AI to assist with routine citation/research drafting is category C; the documented fallout is credibility damage and a report revision with no fine or lawsuit mentioned, so reputational.

codings.one_line: ZeroEyes' AI surveillance system flagged a student's clarinet as a rifle, triggering a school lockdown and police search.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: ZeroEyes is a passive video-surveillance weapon-detection classifier, not a conversational or agentic system the flagged student was interacting with, so it falls outside the rubric's covered system types.
